definition: Continuous sinus rhythm frequency measured in beats per minute (bpm).
sourceOrg: NASA Flight Medicine / ESA Space Medicine
citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 §4.1 (Crew Physical Health); Hughson et al., 'Cardiovascular regulation in microgravity,' J Appl Physiol, 2018 (PMID: 29351474).
appImplementation: Primary vital card #01, Lead-II oscilloscope canvas, Rule CDSS-HR-01 trigger.
limitations: Prototype displays simulated 1 Hz telemetry; does not substitute for real-time 12-lead diagnostic telemetry.

definition: Root Mean Square of Successive Differences (RMSSD) between adjacent R-R intervals reflecting parasympathetic autonomic tone.
citation: Baevsky et al., 'Autonomic cardiovascular regulation in spaceflight,' Acta Astronautica, 2011 (PMID: 21802909); NASA LSDA-0042 Research Archive.
appImplementation: Sub-metric in Cardiovascular card, recovery marker post-exercise.
limitations: Estimated from simulated interbeat intervals; cannot establish clinical arrhythmia diagnosis.

definition: Percentage of arterial hemoglobin oxygenation measured non-invasively via dual-wavelength optical pulse oximetry.
sourceOrg: NASA / FAA Civil Aerospace Medical Institute / Clinical Guidelines
citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 Rev F §6.2.1.2 defines inspired ambient pO2 (19.5–23.1 kPa); FAA CAMI Hypoxia Training Concepts (general physiology context); WHO/AHA Clinical Pulse Oximetry Guidelines.
appImplementation: Primary vital card #02, Rule CDSS-O2-01 trigger, EVA Hypoxia scenario playback.
limitations: Prototype design assumption: SpO2 < 92.0% is an illustrative demonstration trigger adopted for this software prototype. NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 Rev F §6.2.1.2 establishes ambient inspired pO2 limits (19.5–23.1 kPa / 146–173 mmHg) rather than an arterial blood SpO2 threshold. The 92% setting is not an official NASA or FAA standard, nor a clinical diagnosis or validated flight rule. In flight, cold vasoconstriction or sensor motion can cause false drops.

definition: Continuous breathing frequency per minute derived from chest impedance plethysmography.
citation: Canadian Space Agency (CSA) Bio-Monitor Astroskin Flight Validation, ISS Expedition 58/59; NPJ Microgravity, 2021.
appImplementation: Primary vital card #03, Respiratory waveform interpolation, concordance cross-check with SpO₂.
limitations: Synthetically interpolated from 1 Hz CSV data; physical speech or swallowing artifacts are not simulated.

concept: Systemic Blood Pressure & Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP)
definition: Hydrostatic pressure exerted by circulating blood upon systemic arterial walls. MAP = DBP + 1/3(SBP - DBP).
citation: Norsk et al., 'Fluid shifts and cardiovascular regulation in spaceflight,' Physiol Rep, 2015 (PMID: 25895781).
appImplementation: Cardiovascular detail card, fluid shift model in Body Map.
limitations: Indirectly estimated from baseline parameters; true continuous arterial pressure requires continuous finger-cuff photoplethysmography.

definition: Continuous deep body temperature exhibiting a chronic ~1.0°C upward shift during long-duration microgravity.
sourceOrg: Charité Berlin / DLR / ESA Space Medicine
citation: Stahn et al., 'Increased core body temperature in astronauts during long-duration space missions,' Sci Rep, 2017 (DOI: 10.1038/s41598-017-15560-0).
appImplementation: Primary vital card #04, exertional workout thermal tracking.
limitations: Simulated telemetry; operational spaceflight measurement requires double-sensor heat-flux forehead probes.

definition: Atmospheric CO₂ partial pressure and concentration inside spacecraft pressurized volume. At 760 mmHg, 0.31% vol corresponds to 2.36 mmHg.
citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 Rev F §6.2.1.3 (Inspired Partial Pressure of CO2); Law et al., 'Relationship Between CO2 Levels and Headaches on ISS,' J Occup Environ Med, 2014 (PMID: 24806723).
appImplementation: Vital card #04 badge, Rule CDSS-ENV-01, Environmental telemetry monitor.
limitations: Assumes standard total pressure of 760 mmHg (101.3 kPa). Deep-space vessels operating at 8.2 psi (56.5 kPa) require re-calculated partial pressures.

definition: Absorbed and equivalent dosimetric flux from Galactic Cosmic Rays and Solar Particle Events.
nominalRange: ISS LEO: 0.35 – 0.50 mSv/day; Deep Space Transit: 1.50 – 2.00 mSv/day; SPE Alert: > 5.00 mSv/day
citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 §4.4 (Permissible Exposure Limits) & Vol 2 Rev F §11.1 (Ionizing Radiation Protection); Cucinotta et al., NASA/TP-2013-217375.
appImplementation: Environmental badge, Scenario 4 (Solar Storm Flare) playback, storm shelter alert.
limitations: Illustrative sensor values; actual mission biodosimetry requires active silicon detectors and physical tissue equivalent proportional counters.

definition: Ultrasonographic retrobulbar subarachnoid sheath width reflecting cephalad fluid shift and orbital compartmentalization.
nominalRange: Nominal: 4.5 – 5.5 mm; Elevated research threshold: > 5.8 mm
sourceOrg: NASA Human Research Program (HRP) SANS Element
citation: Lee et al., 'Spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome,' NPJ Microgravity, 2020 (DOI: 10.1038/s41526-020-00115-z); NASA HRP SANS Evidence Report.
appImplementation: Body Map (Eyes / SANS), Rule CDSS-SANS-01, Ophthalmic inspection modal.
limitations: Illustrative ultrasound research threshold. In terrestrial medicine ONSD > 5.8 mm indicates elevated ICP; in spaceflight SANS, retrobulbar sheath distension reflects cephalad venous stasis and localized orbital CSF compartmentation without systemic malignant intracranial hypertension.

definition: Fluid pressure of aqueous humor within the globe measured via tonometry.
sourceOrg: NASA HRP / Ophthalmology Clinical Working Group
citation: Mader et al., 'Optic disc edema, globe flattening, and hyperopic shifts in astronauts,' Ophthalmology, 2011 (PMID: 21849212).
appImplementation: Body Map (Eyes stat #02), SANS progression score.
limitations: Single-point values; does not capture circadian IOP fluctuation or trabecular outflow resistance.

definition: Near-infrared interferometric optical cross-sections measuring Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer (RNFL) thickness.
nominalRange: Total average RNFL thickness: 85 – 110 µm; Papilledema alert: > 125 µm
sourceOrg: NASA HRP / Houston Methodist Eye Center
citation: Patel et al., 'OCT imaging of optic disc edema in astronauts,' JAMA Ophthalmol, 2018 (PMID: 29327058).
appImplementation: Body Map (Eyes stat #03), SANS structural evaluation card.
limitations: Digital visualization of clinical findings; software does not process raw OCT B-scan raw raster interferometry files.

definition: Dynamic correlated color temperature (CCT) and photopic lux protocols via Solid-State Light Assemblies.
nominalRange: Wake: 6500K blue-enriched (> 400 lx); Pre-sleep: 2700K warm amber (< 100 lx)
sourceOrg: NASA Human Factors & Habitability / Thomas Jefferson University
citation: Brainard et al., 'Solid-state light assemblies on the ISS for circadian entrainment,' Curr Biol, 2016 (PMID: 27889264); NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 §8.8.
appImplementation: Habitability panel, Crew sleep schedule optimizer.
limitations: Illustrative schedule; does not measure biological melatonin or dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO).

definition: Areal Bone Mineral Density (aBMD) preservation rate in weight-bearing skeletal regions under heavy loading.
nominalRange: Target: > 95.0% baseline retention; Unmitigated spaceflight loss rate: ~1.0-1.5% per month
sourceOrg: NASA Bone Discipline / JSC Human Adaptation & Countermeasures
citation: Sibonga et al., 'Recovery of bone density after long-duration spaceflight,' J Bone Miner Res, 2017 (PMID: 28556391).
appImplementation: Body Map (Spine & Bone), Mission Readiness Pillar #1.
limitations: Mathematical model of bone loading; actual BMD assessment requires dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) pre/post flight.

definition: 10-minute visual Psychomotor Vigilance Task measuring sustained attention and behavioral alertness.
nominalRange: Mean reaction time: < 250 ms (Optimal); Lapses (> 500 ms): <= 2 per 3-min session
sourceOrg: University of Pennsylvania / NASA Behavioral Health & Performance
citation: Basner et al., 'Psychomotor vigilance testing on the International Space Station,' Aerosp Med Hum Perform, 2015 (PMID: 26099342).
appImplementation: Body Map (Brain stat #01), Mission Readiness Pillar #2, Neurocognitive status.
limitations: Static test indicator; does not administer an active millisecond-accurate user reaction test in browser.

definition: Daily prescribed mechanical load to attenuate microgravity-induced musculoskeletal and cardiovascular deconditioning.
nominalRange: ARED: up to 600 lbs simulated load; CEVIS: 150 – 220 Watts at 75–85% VO2 peak
citation: English et al., 'High-intensity resistive and aerobic exercise preserves muscle mass in spaceflight,' NPJ Microgravity, 2020 (DOI: 10.1038/s41526-020-00110-4).
appImplementation: Scenario 3 (ARED Workout) playback, Musculoskeletal countermeasure steps.
limitations: Simulated workout data; does not log physical load cell telemetry from actual gym hardware.

definition: External subatmospheric pressure applied to caudal body segments to induce footward venous fluid redistribution.
nominalRange: Protocol: -20 to -35 mmHg for 30–60 minutes daily
sourceOrg: UC San Diego / NASA HRP / ESA Space Medicine
citation: Hargens et al., 'Lower body negative pressure as a countermeasure for spaceflight deconditioning,' Front Physiol, 2021 (DOI: 10.3389/fphys.2021.722359).
appImplementation: Body Map (Fluid Shift countermeasure), Scenario 5 recovery phase.
limitations: Simulated countermeasure efficacy; individual cardiovascular tolerance and presyncopal risk vary.
